chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the nose, when its stump is eradicated, is the complete wergild; and regarding the eye, when it is blinded, is half the wergild; and regarding the ear, when it is cut, is half the wergild; and regarding the hand, is half the wergild; and regarding the manhood, when it is cut off from the place of the tip, is the complete wergild.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal compensation (diyah) for specific bodily injuries like loss of the nose, eye, or ear?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific financial compensations (diyah) for non-fatal bodily injuries, establishing a clear hierarchy of value based on the severity and function of the affected body part. It distinguishes between injuries warranting the full wergild, such as the complete removal of the nose or the penis, and those requiring half the wergild, including the loss of an eye, ear, or hand. This classification reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on precise quantification of damages in cases of 'udm' (injury) and 'jarh' (wound).
